high_consensus.description: This is a real operational gap: FR-4 and FR-7 can impact every session and write path, so explicit rollback steps are high-ROI and low-cost to document.
Clear prioritization and dependency ordering is missing and materially affects sequencing risk; this is highly actionable and should be added.
Current success criteria are not measurable enough; adding baselines, measurement method, and timeout behavior is essential for objective acceptance.
Conflict handling for allowed-tools is under-specified and likely to cause regressions; defining escalation/override behavior is valuable though somewhat policy-heavy.

disputed.description: This targets the core feasibility risk of FR-7; without a concrete signal for active skill context, the design may be non-implementable.

blockers.concern: Agent-based compliance hook has no failure-mode policy (timeout/error/unavailable)
blockers.why_matters: FR-7 introduces a blocking hook in the critical write path. If the subagent fails or times out, write operations may deadlock or become inconsistent, causing severe developer friction.
blockers.recommendation: Specify deterministic fail-open/fail-closed behavior, timeout budget tiers, circuit breaker logic, and telemetry for hook error rates.

blockers.concern: Assumption that aliasing deprecated models to Opus 4.6 is behaviorally safe
blockers.why_matters: Model substitution may change output quality, latency, and cost unexpectedly. Teams relying on old model behavior may experience regressions despite registry validation passing.
blockers.recommendation: Add explicit user-facing warnings on alias resolution, capture cost/latency deltas, and define acceptance thresholds for output parity before auto-mapping.

blockers.concern: No phased rollout or feature flags for FR-1/FR-2 behavior changes
blockers.why_matters: Adding restrictive `allowed-tools` and `context: fork` can silently break core workflows across multiple downstream projects. Without staged rollout, one bad frontmatter change can halt operator productivity.
blockers.recommendation: Add per-skill feature flags and canary rollout (e.g., enable on 1-2 skills first), plus rollback criteria and a disable switch in config.

blockers.concern: Path-scoped rule extraction risks moving critical safeguards out of always-on context
blockers.why_matters: If globs do not match all relevant files or multi-file tasks, compliance and safety guidance may not load when needed. This can create silent policy gaps.
blockers.recommendation: Create a mandatory core-rules file that remains always loaded, plus rule coverage tests against representative repo paths and edge-case filenames.

blockers.concern: Security boundary for `Bash(pattern *)` is under-specified and potentially bypassable
blockers.why_matters: Pattern-based Bash allowlists are easy to misconfigure and can permit command expansion or unsafe args. This weakens the intended least-privilege model and can reintroduce write/exfiltration risk.
blockers.recommendation: Define a strict command policy format (command + arg schema), ban shell metacharacters by default, and add negative security tests for bypass attempts.
